item.title: #3589007: composer reinstall and composer install --no-dev delete ai_best_practices.yaml and block the plugin
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3589007 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Running composer reinstall drupal/ai_best_practices or composer install --no-dev (when the package is a dev requirement) no longer wipes the project's ai_best_practices.yaml or the plugin's entries in composer.json. Before the fix, those commands removed the package's allow-plugins entry, so the next composer install failed with a "plugin blocked by your allow-plugins config" error, and any customizations in ai_best_practices.yaml were lost. Cleanup still runs on a real composer remove.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Composer calls PluginInterface::uninstall() for the first half of a reinstall and for dev packages dropped by --no-dev, not only when the package is removed. AiBestPracticesPlugin::uninstall() now calls a new private packageStaysInstalled() and returns early, with a verbose-only message, if it reports true. The check relies on Composer writing the lock (or holding it in memory with lock: false) before running package operations, so the lock reflects the post-command project. It looks for the package name in the lock's packages and packages-dev sections. If there is no usable lock, or reading it throws, it falls back to the root package's require and require-dev. Transitive installs are covered because the lock lists them too. A new AiBestPracticesPluginUninstallTest covers the behavior.

Upgrade

If a project already hit this and the allow-plugins entry was removed, restore it with composer config allow-plugins.drupal/ai_best_practices true (the entry the issue says gets removed), or follow the workaround in #3588983 of deleting vendor/drupal/ai_best_practices and running composer install.

item.title: #3583075: Rename ContextDefinitionNormalizer now that it normalizes input and output definitions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583075 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Tool module's JSON Schema builder for input and output definitions is renamed from ContextDefinitionNormalizer to InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer. The old name described core's context system, which the definition families no longer build on. The old class name and service ID keep working for one release but trigger deprecation notices. Behavior is unchanged. Custom code that extends the class, uses its constants, or injects it by service ID should switch to the new names before rc1.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The JSON Schema normalizer for input and output definitions is now Drupal\tool\Normalizer\InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer, with the same DECIMAL_PATTERN and DERIVED_ENUM_LIMIT constants.
  • Deprecation: Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer and the tool.normalizer.context_definition service are deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta12 and removed from tool:1.0.0-rc1. Use InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer and tool.normalizer.input_output_definition.

Technical details

The full implementation moved into src/Normalizer/InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer.php. Its docblock now names the input and output definition families as the subject. Core ContextDefinitionInterface support is described as the ai module's override path. ContextDefinitionNormalizer stays as a thin shell that extends the new class. Its constructor calls @trigger_error() with E_USER_DEPRECATED, and its docblock carries @deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta12 and is removed from tool:1.0.0-rc1.

In tool.services.yml the service is now tool.normalizer.input_output_definition, still tagged normalizer with priority 100. tool.normalizer.context_definition stays as a private alias with a deprecated message. Normalizers are private services, so the old ID resolves only where another service definition injects it by ID. A new kernel test, ContextDefinitionNormalizerDeprecationTest, covers the class and alias deprecations. Internal references were updated: LegacyTypedDataNormalizer uses InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer::DECIMAL_PATTERN, and comments in EntityHandleTransformer and EffectiveDataDefinition plus NormalizerFormatRestrictionTest were changed to match. The issue body says tool_belt, canvas_tools and mcp_server_tool_bridge do not refer to the old class or service ID.

Upgrade

Replace the class and service references:

// Before
use Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer;
// After
use Drupal\tool\Normalizer\InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer;

# Before
arguments: ['@tool.normalizer.context_definition']
# After
arguments: ['@tool.normalizer.input_output_definition']

item.title: #3589004: Eval runner: add a Kiro CLI provider
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3589004 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Behavioral evals can now run against Kiro CLI as well as claude, codex, gemini and mistral. Run python3 evals/run-evals.py --behavioral --skill <skill> --provider kiro to see whether a skill changes Kiro's answers. Kiro runs answer-only with no tools trusted. It needs kiro-cli 2.31 or later, and you log in with kiro-cli login or set KIRO_API_KEY. Kiro reports credits rather than tokens, so runs show no token or cost figures.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New kiro provider for the behavioral eval runner (--provider kiro, Inspect model string abp_cli/kiro), default model claude-sonnet-5.

Technical details

The provider is run_kiro() in evals/providers.py, registered in PROVIDERS, PROVIDER_DEFAULTS and ISOLATION_MODES. It calls kiro-cli chat --agent-engine v3 --no-interactive --trust-tools= --output-format stream-json --model <model> from a fresh temporary directory. The merged code differs from the issue text: the prompt goes on stdin rather than after --, which also avoids Kiro parsing the skill's --- frontmatter as an option. The output is stream-json, not plain text. The default model is claude-sonnet-5, not auto, because auto picks a model per task and runs would not compare.

Older kiro-cli releases leave their agent server running with the inherited stdout, so stdout and stderr go to temp files, the process is started in its own session, and the whole process group is killed after wait(). The answer comes from the runFinished event's finalText. If that is truncated or missing, the agent_message_chunk updates are joined instead.

Each call gets a throwaway KIRO_HOME, so the operator's ~/.kiro steering, skills and agents do not load. _kiro_context() reads the steering from the session log under KIRO_HOME and the skills and agents from the stream's command list. It raises ContextLeakError for anything that is not bundled with Kiro, or when no session log exists. Per the docs, kiro-cli 2.16 still read ~/.kiro with KIRO_HOME set, so it is unsupported. test_scoring.py tests this against a fake kiro-cli. CONTRIBUTING.md, evals/inspect/README.md and evals/inspect/to_eee.py were updated for the new provider.

Upgrade

Install kiro-cli 2.31 or later, then run:

python3 evals/run-evals.py --behavioral --skill drupal-automated-testing --provider kiro

item.title: #3594805: Eval Commons schemas are out of date with the 1.1.x targets
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594805 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

The ai_eval portable schemas (Eval Commons) now match what the 1.1.x targets actually do. Exported workflow runs get a real identity instead of unknown, and the schema URLs no longer point at a non-existent 1.0.x branch. A new decision rubric schema is added, and the schema README and examples are brought up to date. The five Northmoor sample datasets already validated and still do. The old schemas and 404 URLs stay on main until 1.1.x merges back.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Exported workflow runs are now identified as drupal-workflow/<engine>/<workflow_id> in model_info and evaluation_id; schema $id URLs moved from raw/1.0.x/ to raw/1.1.0-alpha1/.
  • New API: New schema/decision_rubric.schema.json for the portable decision rubric; a rubric judge declaration may omit model_id to use the site judge model.

Technical details

In ResultEnvelopeBuilder, a workflow-mode run now reads workflow_engine, workflow_id, workflow_snapshot and workflow_output_path from the run snapshot, falling back to the run config. When engine and id are set, model_info is drupal-workflow/<engine>/<workflow_id> and evaluation_id is built from it. Rows recorded before this change have no workflow keys, so they fall through to the previous agent-id branch and keep their original evaluation_id. The issue also says the recorded workflow now runs on every step of a stepped run. I did not verify that part in the diff.

Schema changes: dataset.schema.json descriptions are corrected for multi-turn, caller_uid (also the account a workflow runs as), user_name and inputs. Expected outputs for automator and taxonomy targets are documented as expected.<name>, checked with target_match. Per the issue, expected.items ids must name a datasource, so bare ids like 108 are rejected (new invalid example dataset-retrieval-items-bare-id.yaml). decision_rubric.schema.json is new: it requires question and rules, and describes the grader as scoring 0 to 100, counting at most two errors per rule.

$id values now name the release that ships the file (raw/1.1.0-alpha1/), and editor headers name the branch (raw/1.1.x/). The issue says a test keeps $id off branch names. schema/README.md and the docs are rewritten to list all four schemas plus the new one, which check kinds have executors, the runtime validation, and the targets with the fields they read. New valid and invalid examples cover automator fields, taxonomy labels, the decision rubric, and failure taxonomy modes.

Upgrade

If you copy the schemas or use editor headers in your own dataset or rubric YAML files, point them at the new URLs (raw/1.1.x/schema/... for editor headers). Any bare retrieval ids in expected.items need to be changed to ids that name a datasource. Consumers that match on exported workflow model_info or evaluation_id will see drupal-workflow/<engine>/<workflow_id> for new runs instead of unknown.

item.title: #3586791: Add Refusal Answer type to support OpenAI Decision API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586791 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

The AI module's Decision operation can now represent a model declining to answer an individual question. Previously a refusal, which OpenAI's Decision API can return, was treated as broken output and failed the whole response. Models that declare the new decision_refusals capability may now refuse single questions while the other answers stay usable. Refusals from models that don't declare it still count as broken output.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AnswerValidation::forQuestion() gains an optional third parameter $allow_refusal (default FALSE); AnswerFactory::fromArray() accepts a refusal type.
  • New API: New RefusalAnswer value, AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals, AiDecisionRefusedException, and DecisionResponse::isRefused() / getRefusals().

Technical details

A new final class Drupal\ai\OperationType\Decision\Value\RefusalAnswer implements AnswerInterface. Its type is 'refusal' (RefusalAnswer::TYPE), getRaw() keeps the provider's wire data, and toArray() returns only ['type' => 'refusal']. AnswerFactory::fromArray() gains a refusal case.

AnswerValidation::forQuestion() takes a third parameter bool $allow_refusal = FALSE. A RefusalAnswer is accepted for any question type when it is TRUE, and otherwise throws \InvalidArgumentException. DecisionValidationEventSubscriber::postGenerate() only resolves the model's capabilities when the answer is a refusal. It checks the provider's getDecisionCapabilities() for AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals. If the provider or model can't be resolved, it counts as not declared, and the InvalidArgumentException becomes AiBrokenOutputException.

On DecisionResponse, isRefused($id) and getRefusals() (question ids) were added. getNoul(), getChoice() and getScore() now throw the new AiDecisionRefusedException (an \UnexpectedValueException implementing AiExceptionInterface) when the question was refused, instead of the type-mismatch error. The capability's enum value is decision_refusals, in the decision operation type group.

Upgrade

Provider authors whose Decision API can decline a question should declare the capability and return a refusal answer:

AiModelCapability::DecisionRefusals
// wire answer: ['type' => 'refusal', ...]; AnswerFactory::fromArray() turns it into RefusalAnswer

Callers of DecisionResponse should check isRefused($id) or getRefusals() before calling getNoul(), getChoice() or getScore(), or catch AiDecisionRefusedException.

item.title: #3589000: drupal-a11y-dynamic recommends FocusCommand, which does not exist in core (use FocusFirstCommand)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3589000 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The drupal-a11y-dynamic skill in AI Best Practices told agents to return focus after AJAX responses with \Drupal\Core\Ajax\FocusCommand, a class core does not have. Code generated from it would fail when the AJAX response was built. The skill and its evals now point to core's FocusFirstCommand, and the skill notes that a heading or landmark used as a focus target needs tabindex="-1".

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The skill's SKILL.md now uses FocusFirstCommand in its frontmatter description, the AJAX focus section and its code example, the inline-error example and the "What not to do" section. It describes the command as taking a container selector. Focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the container, or to the container itself if that is focusable. Otherwise focus stays on the triggering element, which is why heading or landmark targets need tabindex="-1".

The evals had locked in the wrong class. In the rubric for case B02, FocusFirstCommand moves into must_contain_any, and new FocusCommand( and Ajax\FocusCommand are listed under must_not_contain, so an answer using the nonexistent class now fails. The dataset criteria, the README.md and the static check (S06) text are updated to match.

item.title: #3586784: Let Decision models declare a minimum number of choice options
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586784 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

Decision providers can now declare a minimum number of options for choice questions. Some backends need at least two options and previously could only fail after a round trip to the server, because the shared contract suite assumed a single option was valid. With a declared minimum, a choice question with too few options is rejected with AiBadRequestException before anything is sent. The provider's capability details now show the minimum next to the maximum. Existing declarations keep working unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: DecisionCapabilities gains a trailing nullable constructor argument and public property minChoiceOptions (NULL means unknown, a single option is accepted).

Technical details

DecisionCapabilities takes ?int $minChoiceOptions = NULL as the last constructor argument. The constructor throws \InvalidArgumentException if a minimum is set without DecisionChoice support, is below 1, or exceeds maxChoiceOptions. DecisionRequestValidator::validate() calls a new private checkMinimum() for choice questions, throwing AiBadRequestException ("supplied N choice options; the minimum is M") before the existing maximum check. An unknown (NULL) minimum is left to the provider.

DecisionCapabilityDetails::limits() now prints "Choice options: minimum X, maximum Y" (or "maximum Y", or "not supported" when choice is not declared). It also reports "not supported" for score levels when score is not declared. The markup string changed from "Maximum choice options: ..." to "Choice options: ...".

On the test side, DecisionContractCases builds choice questions with max(1, minChoiceOptions) options. boundaries() adds an accepted choices/<min> case and a rejected choices/<min - 1> case when the minimum is above 1. DecisionProviderContractTestBase::testDecisionDeclarationsAndDiscovery() now compares minChoiceOptions too. docs/developers/decision_provider_contract.md and call_decision.md document the limit.

Upgrade

Providers whose models need more than one choice option can declare it in their capabilities, for example:

new DecisionCapabilities([Capability::DecisionChoice], maxChoiceOptions: 26, minChoiceOptions: 2)

Providers that currently map a server 4xx for too few options can drop that workaround.

item.title: #3585947: Multi-round elicitation fails on protocol 2026-07-28 without a request state signing key
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585947 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

On MCP protocol 2026-07-28, a tool that asks the client more than one question in a single tools/call used to fail on the second question with a "could not carry its own state" internal error. The module now signs the state that carries earlier answers between rounds, so multi-round elicitation works. No new setting is needed. Tools that elicit only once were not affected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Under 2026-07-28 there are no server-to-client requests. ClientGateway::elicit() ends the call with an InputRequiredResult, the client resends the whole call, and the tool reruns from the top. Earlier answers travel in a signed requestState. The SDK needs an HMAC key from Builder::setRequestState(), which McpServerFactory never called.

McpServerFactory now takes @private_key as a new last constructor argument (mcp_server.services.yml is updated). It calls $builder->setRequestState() with Crypt::hmacBase64('mcp_server.request_state', $this->privateKey->get() . Settings::getHashSalt()). This is the same derivation style as core's CsrfTokenGenerator. The key comes from secrets shared across web heads, so a retry can land on any of them. The call is wrapped in method_exists($builder, 'setRequestState'), because mcp/sdk 0.7 predates this protocol version and has no such method.

Rotating the private key or hash salt only invalidates multi-round calls in progress. The issue cites the SDK's 10-minute TTL for this state. The commit adds a fixture tool, ElicitingTwiceTool, and a 2026-07-28 tools/call test in McpServerFunctionalTest that answers both rounds.

item.title: #3583032: Split title from description in the JSON Schema instead of prefixing the label onto every description
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583032 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

Tool API's generated JSON Schema no longer prepends the label to every description. A member with the label "Title" and the docblock text "Gets the title." used to be advertised with \"description\": \"Title: Gets the title.\". It now gets \"description\": \"Gets the title.\", and the label stays in title. This changes the prompt text of every tool's inputs and outputs. Any client, test or documentation that matches the old Label: description strings needs updating. The issue asks for a mention in the 1.0.0 release notes.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ContextDefinitionNormalizer::getDescription() now returns the definition's description only, with no Label: prefix (and NULL when empty).

Technical details

The change is in ContextDefinitionNormalizer::getDescription() in src/Normalizer/ContextDefinitionNormalizer.php. It now returns (string) $definition->getDescription() ?: NULL. A definition with no description therefore emits no description key, and the label travels only as title. The comment that deferred this split to a follow-up issue was replaced with one saying the label goes out as the title only.

The multiple branch already blanked the item definition's label and description before normalizing items. I did not see a change to it in the commit I read. With getDescription() fixed, the author's text lands on the array and items carries a description only when something adds one, such as the entity handle hints "(pass a handle from a previous tool call)" and "(returns a handle for use in subsequent tool calls)". Most of the diff is test expectation updates: InputSchemaMatrixTest, MultipleListSchemaTest, RicherSchemaEmissionTest, ListDescriptionSchemaTest, MethodToolTest, ToolComplexEventTransformTest and ToolDefinitionNormalizeTest. I did not check the documentation examples that the issue's task list mentions.

Upgrade

Update any code or tests that assert on the old prefixed text. For example:

// Before.
$this->assertSame('Tags: Words that describe the album.', $schema['description']);
// After.
$this->assertSame('Words that describe the album.', $schema['description']);

Read the label from title if a consumer needs it.

item.title: #3594799: Grade taxonomy automators with auto-create without saving terms
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594799 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval field automator target (#3594787) used to refuse taxonomy rules whose field has auto-create on, because running them saves a new term for every label that has no match. That left tagging automators on such sites untested. They can now be graded. The run captures the labels the rule would store and grades those, without saving any terms. It also records which labels match existing terms and which would be new.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The rule runs as usual. The labels it produced are taken just before storage, and the rule is stopped from storing them, so no term is saved. The labels the field would have received are graded, with each one recorded as matching an existing term or as a would-be new term. A separate guard blocks term saves for the whole run. The run fails rather than storing anything when the labels cannot be taken safely. This is a child of #3594785. The fix diff was not available to me and the merged code is not in the cloned repository, so this description comes from the issue body only. I could not verify class or hook names.

item.title: #3594791: Let each question pass its own inputs to a workflow target
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594791 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In AI Eval, a question in a dataset can now set its own inputs for a workflow target. Put a map of port name to value under the question's metadata.inputs. It overrides the target's fixed inputs for the same ports. One target can then cover questions that need different values, such as a language or a length limit, so you no longer need a target for each combination. Bad input is refused before the workflow starts. The question editor keeps these inputs as a typed map when you save.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Question metadata.inputs (map of workflow port to value) is read by workflow targets and described in schema/dataset.schema.json.

Technical details

EvalRunner::invokeWorkflow() now builds the workflow inputs in three layers. First come the target's fixed workflow_inputs. The question's metadata.inputs goes over them with array_replace(), so the question wins on the same key and values keep their types. The question port is set last, so nothing else can override it. The workflow arm of the question dispatch passes $question['metadata']['inputs']. Chat and agent modes ignore it.

Validation happens before launch, and failures are recorded as refused. A new questionInputs() helper accepts NULL, a string-keyed map, or a JSON object string. It rejects lists and empty or non-string keys. A metadata.inputs key that matches the question port is refused. The runner's inputPorts() is called, and an exception from it is also a refusal. When the workflow declares ports, the question port and every fixed or per-question input must be one of them. The refusal message lists the declared ports. A workflow that declares no ports takes any names as given.

For the editor, DatasetQuestionEditor::assemble() decodes the JSON text in metadata.inputs and stores it as a map. An empty {} or [] is dropped. Nested empty objects are refused, because dataset storage cannot tell {} from [] once decoded. DatasetQuestionEditor::inputsError() gives a readable message for this, and DatasetQuestionController and GuidedTestController call it. A question with metadata.inputs stays editable instead of read-only. schema/dataset.schema.json declares metadata.inputs as an object. The same commit also adds the ai_eval_ai_answers submodule and moves tool-call recording into Workflow\ToolCallRecord. Those are not part of this issue.

Upgrade

Per-question inputs are set in the dataset. For example, schema/examples/valid/dataset-workflow-inputs.yaml is a working example. A question carries metadata.inputs such as {"language": "el"}, keyed by the workflow's input port names.

item.title: #3594796: Add a settings form and a requirements check for the content review judge
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594796 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The content review judge in ai_eval_content_review now has a settings form at /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/content-review for the review rule, criterion, content type, body field and text format. It offers only choices that exist on the site. Previously these could only be changed with drush cset or config import, and a content type without the expected body field (as on a Drupal CMS page) made the criterion see only the title and score the answer 0 with no warning. Now a judge with settings that do not fit the site reports the answer as not measured, and the status report says what is wrong. New installs leave the content type, body field and text format unset, so a site owner must choose them before the judge can run. Existing sites keep their current values.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New installs ship ai_eval_content_review.settings with bundle, body_field and body_format empty (previously page, body, basic_html); existing sites keep their values.
  • Permission change: New route /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/content-review is gated by the existing administer ai eval permission.
  • New API: New JudgeSettingsChecker service (ai_eval_content_review.settings_checker) with problems() and errors(); CriterionRunner takes it as a fifth constructor argument.

Technical details

A single JudgeSettingsChecker is shared by the form, the status report and the judge. problems() returns errors and warnings keyed by setting. Errors cover a missing rule, a missing criterion index, a missing or nonexistent content type, a body field that is unset, absent or not of type text, text_long or text_with_summary, an unset, nonexistent or disabled text format, a format the field's allowed_formats excludes, and extra_fields the type lacks. A warning is raised for a disabled rule, or for a rule that does not apply to the configured bundle. errors() returns only the blocking messages.

CriterionRunner::review() calls errors() before building the unsaved node. If any are returned it throws a RuntimeException ("The content review judge settings do not fit this site: ..."), so the judge records no measurement instead of reviewing a page without the answer. JudgeSettingsRequirements (hook_runtime_requirements) adds a status report row: "Not set up" (warning) when no rule is set, "Settings fit this site" (OK), "Check the settings" (warning) or "Cannot review" (error). JudgeSettingsForm is a ConfigFormBase that filters the criterion, body field and format selects by the chosen rule, content type and field, and redraws them with htmx. It warns when the criterion changes, since existing judges then check another criterion and need validating again. Earlier validations are not marked stale. The default config/install values for bundle, body_field and body_format are now empty strings.

Upgrade

Custom code that constructs CriterionRunner directly must pass the new ai_eval_content_review.settings_checker service (JudgeSettingsChecker) as the fifth argument. On new installs, open /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/content-review and choose the content type, body field and text format before running the judge.

item.title: #3594795: Judge content review criteria without saving a node
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594795 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The AI Eval content review judge no longer saves and deletes a temporary unpublished node for every judged answer. The page is built in memory and reviewed without being saved, so automators, search indexing and other save hooks stop running per answer. That removes the extra LLM call per judged answer and the search index warning for the deleted node. Records made by the judge are visible only to users with "configure reviews" and are hidden from the AI Content Review review queue. A criterion that needs a saved entity cannot be judged this way.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: ai_eval_content_review now depends on the entity module.
  • Database update: ai_eval_content_review_update_10001() installs the ai_eval_page review record bundle with an eval_key field.
  • Permission change: Records of type ai_eval_page and their suggestions require "configure reviews" to view, and are hidden from the AI Content Review review queue.
  • API change: CriterionRunner constructor takes a new fourth argument, the ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages service (EvalPageRegistry).

Technical details

AI Content Review's internal record type reloads the reviewed entity by id, so it cannot review an unsaved one. The submodule now ships its own review_record bundle plugin, ai_eval_page, with an eval_key bundle field. CriterionRunner::review() builds the node with create() and does not save it. It wraps the node and a random key in a new EvalPage value object, which is deliberately not an entity because the internal record type claims every entity. The EvalPage is registered in a request-scoped EvalPageRegistry (service ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages) and passed to the real ReviewOrchestrator::runCriterion(). The record type looks the page up by key. It gives the criterion the same review context lines as for a saved node, with the node as its node token context, and it applies no rules and refuses suggestions. In a finally block, deleteReviews() removes the records and their suggestions by eval_key, and the page is removed from the registry.

Access: AI Content Review alpha3 checks the reviewed subject only for records about a Drupal entity, so ai_eval_page records and their suggestions would be viewable with "view review records". EvalPageAccess forbids view, update and delete of them, and of their suggestions, without "configure reviews". Two pages in AI Content Review do not check entity access. A route subscriber adds JudgedPageRecordAccessCheck to the record detail route (/ai-content-review/record/{record_id}/detail), and a form alter on the review queue removes ai_eval_page rows for everyone and leaves them out of the waiting count.

Limit: the criterion gets an entity with no id. Tools that reload the node by id (for example GetCurrentContentEntityValues) and resumed runs cannot see it. The extra_fields setting still fills extra values on the unsaved node, but automators no longer fill them.

Upgrade

Run database updates. ai_eval_content_review_update_10001() installs the ai_eval_page review record bundle on existing sites. The submodule now also depends on the entity module, which AI Content Review already requires. Code that constructs CriterionRunner directly must pass the new fourth argument, the ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages service:

ai_eval_content_review.eval_pages:
  class: Drupal\ai_eval_content_review\EvalPageRegistry

item.title: #3594794: Add a judge for every criterion of a review rule
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594794 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The AI Eval content review judge now covers every criterion of every AI Content Review rule, not just the one at the site-wide criterion_index. A rule with three criteria such as Tone & voice, Inclusive language and Grammar now has three judges. Existing judges keep their ids, so their scores and validations stay attached to the same criterion. The drush scoring command can target one criterion, and importing a fixture refuses to continue when the criterion at its recorded position has since changed label.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Optional trailing criterion position argument on CriterionRunner::reviewAsJudge(), judgeModel(), editorsModel(), review(), criterion() and ReviewRuleJudges::judgeId(); new content_review_criterion_at__<rule>__<index> judge ids; new --criterion drush option on ai-eval-cr:score-items.

Technical details

ReviewRuleJudges::graderInfoAlter() now loops over every criterion of each review_rule, plus the criterion_index from settings even if the rule has no criterion there. The criterion at that position keeps the existing id (content_review_criterion, or content_review_criterion__<rule> for other rules). All other positions get content_review_criterion_at__<rule>__<index>, counting from 0. This prefix is disjoint from the older ids, so a rule id containing criterion_1 or __ cannot collide with an existing judge. If another module already declares an id, that judge is skipped and a warning is logged. Ids follow positions, as AI Content Review's own {rule}__{index} names do, so reordering a rule's criteria moves its judges. Judge definitions carry criterion_index and criterion_label, and the label reads "Content review: <rule> / <criterion>".

CriterionRunner::reviewAsJudge(), judgeModel(), editorsModel(), review() and criterion(), and ReviewRuleJudges::judgeId(), take an optional trailing criterion position (judgeId() also takes the default index). drush ai-eval-cr:score-items has a new --criterion option (a position from 0, defaulting to the settings value) and writes criterion_index and criterion_label into the fixture meta. import-run rebuilds the judge id from that meta and errors with a request to give --grader when the label now at that position differs from the recorded one. The CHANGELOG notes it cannot distinguish criteria that share a label.

Upgrade

Callers of the listed CriterionRunner methods and ReviewRuleJudges::judgeId() need no change: the new criterion position argument is optional and trailing. To score a non-default criterion from drush:

drush ai-eval-cr:score-items --items=items.yaml --criterion=2 --out=/tmp/out.yaml

Summary

When some questions error out or can't be scored, the pass rate is calculated only over the questions that were measured. The drush run summary and the result detail page now say so next to the pass rate, for example "9 of 12 measured", so a "100%" is no longer easy to read as 100% of all 12 questions. Technical details

In EvalRunCommand, the target result line now carries the count inside the parentheses after the pass rate, such as (pass_rate: 100% [70.1%–100%], 9 of 12 measured: 3 errors) [PASS] 34s. The reasons for missing questions (N errors, N unscored) are listed after the count. This replaces the old trailing (3 errors) / (3 unscored) suffix after the duration. The measured count uses valid_count from the result, falling back to total questions minus errors minus unscored. The same value is reused by the existing insufficient-coverage warning.

In EvalResultsController, the pass-rate cell on the result detail page computes $measuredCount once (question_count - error_count - unscored) and uses it for the existing (passed / total) figure. It appends , N of M measured when $measuredCount is below question_count.
